calls.name: gfx.circle
gfx.clear
calls.prose:
Fill the whole canvas with one palette index, and mark
the shared depth buffer for reset. Nearly every draw starts here; without
it the previous frame shows through wherever this one draws nothing.
Index 0 is the one to choose deliberately: it is the sky, the water, the
room the game happens in.

calls.name: gfx.floor
calls.prose:
Mode-7 textured ground plane (engine v6): sweeps
the loaded terrain colormap per scanline. cfg: x, y, z, yaw, horizon, vy,
vh, focal, dist, fog1, fog2, tscale, sky, far. Fills the same depth
buffer gfx.ssprite z-tests against. false = nothing loaded.

calls.name: gfx.image
calls.prose:
Draw assets/images/{name}.vsp
(a scene or background; engine v2). false when the image is missing.
Integer scale (engine v14, 1..4) draws it nearest-neighbour scaled, the
native-canvas path for backgrounds authored against the classic canvas.

params.name: name
params.constraint: image name only (no path, no extension)

calls.name: gfx.line
calls.prose:
Bresenham, inclusive endpoints, clipped
per pixel, so coordinates off the canvas are safe rather than fatal.

calls.name: gfx.map
calls.prose:
NOT IMPLEMENTED. A no-op that logs once per
app run. Tilemaps were deferred because sprite loops cover what v1 apps
need; the entry stays registered so an app that reaches for it gets nothing
drawn rather than a nil-index crash.

calls.name: gfx.mcam
calls.prose:
Camera for every gfx.mesh (and gfx.vdraw) until the next
call. cfg:
  x, y, z, yaw, pitch  = where the camera is and where it looks
  focal                = pixels per world unit at distance 1
  cx, cy               = projection centre, usually the canvas centre
  tier                 = palette step C adds per lighting tier
                         (stomp's +32/+64 convention, so 32)
  lx, ly, lz           = light direction, normalised
  fog1, fog2           = distance fog (engine v12): a face past fog1 drops
                         one lighting tier, past fog2 two. The SAME two
                         bands gfx.terrain and gfx.floor fade the ground
                         through, so a model recedes into the haze with the
                         world behind it instead of reading as a sticker.
                         0 = off.
  depth                = false skips the per-pixel depth test and fills
                         spans with memset. The test costs 2 PSRAM reads +
                         2 writes per pixel and buys nothing over a FLAT
                         ground, so an app that sorts its models far-to-near
                         should turn it off (~4 ms/frame in Pet Parade).
  ztest                = false (engine v16) still WRITES depth but skips the
                         compare: half the PSRAM traffic, for ground layers
                         the app painter-orders itself. Things that
                         interpenetrate, such as props and the player, keep it.

calls.name: gfx.mesh

signatures.text: gfx.mesh(slot, x, y, z [, yaw [, scale [, pitch [, roll [, tier [, col [, smap [, zbias]]]]]]]])

calls.prose:
One call draws the whole model: transform, near-clip,
backface cull, directional lighting and a z-buffered span fill against the
same depth buffer gfx.terrain / gfx.floor write, so meshes occlude the
ground and each other with no sorting and no popping.

roll spins the model about its own forward axis, because yaw and pitch
together cannot express a barrel roll. tier defaults to -1 = light it; tier >= 0
forces one lighting tier (flat/emissive). col >= 0 overrides every face
colour.

smap (engine v16) > 0 draws the mesh THROUGH that gfx.shademap level,
remapping the framebuffer pixels it covers rather than replacing them,
which is how real translucent shadows and tints are drawn. zbias (engine v16, world units) is a
depth priority: the mesh wins the z-fight against coplanar-ish layers below
it, which is what water over terrain and decals on ground need. Affine
depth interpolation makes big flat layers fight, and tessellating them
alone does not fully fix it.

calls.name: gfx.mload
calls.prose:
Upload a model table (the shape each
tools/assets gen.py emits, and stomp's lib/models.lua hand-builds):
  verts = {{x,y,z}, ...}
  faces = {{a,b,c[,d], col=, nx=, ny=, nz=}, ...}   -- 1-based, d = quad
  parts = { name = {first_face, last_face, px,py,pz}, ... }  -- optional
Geometry is copied into native arrays, so the Lua tables can be dropped
afterwards. Call in vupp.init: it allocates, and the frame budget is real.

Engine v16: load assets/models/
{name}.vmesh straight into the mesh slot, touching zero Lua heap. Model
tables of this size are ~15x their binary weight as Lua objects AND
vupp.import pins whatever it returns for the life of the app, so a
two-thousand-face model as a lib table is a memory bug, not a style
choice. Format (little-endian, the tools/assets gen scripts emit it):
  "VMSH" u8 ver=1, u8 pad, u16 nv, u16 nf,
  nv * 3*f32 xyz,
  nf * { u16 a,b,c,d (0-based, d=0xFFFF triangle); u8 col; i8 nx,ny,nz }
No parts (rigid models); use the table form when a model needs mpose.

calls.name: gfx.mpose

signatures.text: gfx.mpose(slot, part, yaw [, pitch [, dx, dy, dz]])

calls.prose:
Pose one part about
its own pivot, sticky until changed. Parts are 1-based in the order
model.parts iterated at load. This is how a character walks without a
skeleton: swing the leg parts, bob the body.

calls.name: gfx.munload
calls.prose:
Free one mesh slot (engine v15). Lets a
screen-based app swap model sets inside the 16-slot budget; unloading a
slot mid-frame that a queued gfx.mesh still references is the app's bug.

calls.name: gfx.rect

signatures.text: gfx.rect(x, y, w, h, color [, filled])

calls.prose:
(x,y) is the top-left corner.
`filled` defaults to FALSE, so the plain five-argument call draws an
outline; this is the most common surprise in a first app.

calls.name: gfx.shademap
calls.prose:
Register the palette remap texcol applies at
`shade` level 1..7 (0 = no shade): t[i+1] is the index drawn for source
index i. Missing entries keep the identity mapping. Don't map to 255,
transparency is decided before the remap.

calls.name: gfx.sprite
calls.prose:
A cell of
assets/sprites.vsp (engine v2, docs/07). No-op when the app ships no sheet.
Integer scale (engine v14) draws the cell scale x bigger, the native-canvas
path for classic-authored art; routed through the ssprite scaler.

calls.name: gfx.ssprite

signatures.text: gfx.ssprite(cell, x, y, w, h [, flip [, shade [, depth]]])

calls.prose:
Sheet cell
scaled to w x h. depth (world units) z-tests per pixel against the last
gfx.terrain pass so billboards hide behind hills; omit for HUD and the
player character. flip like gfx.sprite ("x"|"y"|"xy").

calls.name: gfx.terrain
calls.prose:
Render the loaded heightfield (engine v4). cfg:
x, y, z, yaw (required-ish; default 0), horizon, vy, vh, focal, dist,
fog1, fog2 (shademap levels 2/3 distance bands), water, wcolor, sky, colw.
Fills the per-pixel depth buffer ssprite z-tests against. false = no
terrain loaded (parallels gfx.image).

calls.name: gfx.texcol

signatures.text: gfx.texcol(x, yTop, h, cell, tx [, shade [, w]])

calls.prose:
One textured vertical
column: texel column tx of sheet cell `cell`, scaled to h on-screen pixels
starting at yTop (engine v3). Transparent texels skip, so billboards draw
column-by-column. No-op when the app ships no sheet, like gfx.sprite.

calls.name: gfx.text
calls.prose:
Size 1, 2 or 3 (default 1), and each
size is its OWN glyph set rather than a scale: 4x6, 8x12 and 12x18 cells,
so big text is drawn at its own resolution instead of upscaled. Advance is
always 4*size px per character and line height 6*size px, so centre with
x = (gfx.w - #str * 4 * size) / 2. Do the arithmetic, do not eyeball it.
"\n" starts a new line.

ASCII 32..127 ONLY. Every other byte draws a literal "?", which bites
hardest exactly where it is most tempting: a star, an arrow, a heart or an
accented name in a score badge. "★ 70" renders as "?70?" because the star
is three bytes. Draw those with gfx.circle / gfx.tri / gfx.rect.

Anything a CHILD reads wants size 3 (size 2 for secondary labels); size 1
is a 4x6 glyph, genuinely unreadable to a five-year-old, and exists for
debug text. Size 3 needs engine v8 and clamps to 2 below that.

calls.name: gfx.theight
calls.prose:
Bilinear terrain height in world units
(movement, camera, billboard feet). 0 when no terrain is loaded.

calls.name: gfx.tload
calls.prose:
Load assets/terrain/{name}_h.vsp +
{name}_c.vsp (square power-of-two planes) into the terrain slot. hscale
converts height bytes to world units (default 0.1). One slot per app run.

params.name: name
params.constraint: terrain name only (no path, no extension)

calls.name: gfx.tri
calls.prose:
flat-shaded triangle (engine v5), any
winding, clipped. Lighting = the app picking a darker palette tier.

calls.name: gfx.vblock
calls.prose:
Palette indices per face. The renderer
adds the lighting tier (gfx.mcam{tier=}) per face direction, so give it the
BASE colour and let the tiers live at +tier / +2*tier as everywhere else.

calls.name: gfx.vbox

signatures.text: gfx.vbox(x, y, z, sx, sy, sz, block)

calls.prose:
Draw one axis-aligned box this frame,
ordered against the world. This is how a third-person character (or, later,
a mob) exists: it cannot be a grid cell because it moves, and it cannot be a
gfx.mesh because the voxel pass owns the span buffer and keeps no depth
buffer for a later pass to test against. (x,y) is the centre, z the base.

calls.name: gfx.vdraw
calls.prose:
Remeshes dirty chunks, then rasterises the whole
world in ONE call through the span buffer: near-to-far, memset only what is
still uncovered. Uses the gfx.mcam camera. No depth buffer is touched, so
anything drawn after this must painter-order itself.

calls.name: gfx.vfill
calls.prose:
Inclusive box. Worldgen goes through
here: a Lua triple loop over even a small world blows the per-callback
instruction budget long before it finishes.

calls.name: gfx.vget
calls.prose:
The block id at one cell, 0 for air. Reading
outside the world is 0 too rather than an error, so collision code can
probe freely at the edges without bounds-checking first.

calls.name: gfx.vline
calls.prose: Flat vertical line, inclusive endpoints.

calls.name: gfx.vload
calls.prose:
Persist the whole block world
(engine v17). Names are [a-z0-9_].
It goes beside the app's documents (not in the app directory, which an
update replaces), so a child's world survives a reinstall. The grid
run-length-encodes itself in C: 368,640 cells is three orders of magnitude
past the 4KB document cap and far past what Lua could walk on device.

calls.name: gfx.vlod
calls.prose:
How far out gfx.vpattern textures still draw (default 40
blocks). A textured span runs a per-pixel loop where a flat one is a
memset, so this is the app's dial between how far the texture reads and
how much of the frame the far field costs. 0 = texture everything.

calls.name: gfx.vpattern
calls.prose:
A 4x4 texture for one block type, the SAME
on all six faces so a block is recognisable from any angle. mask is 16 bits
read row-major (bit 0 = top-left); a set bit draws `accent` instead of the
face colour. Both take the lighting tier, so a patterned block shades like a
flat one. Omit it (or pass mask 0) and the block fills at memset speed.

calls.name: gfx.vray
calls.prose:
The first
solid cell along the ray and the empty cell just before it (break here,
place there). This is the crosshair.

calls.name: gfx.vsave
calls.prose:
Persist the whole block world
(engine v17). Names are [a-z0-9_].
It goes beside the app's documents (not in the app directory, which an
update replaces), so a child's world survives a reinstall. The grid
run-length-encodes itself in C: 368,640 cells is three orders of magnitude
past the 4KB document cap and far past what Lua could walk on device.

calls.name: gfx.vset
calls.prose:
0 = air. Marks the chunk (and any neighbour whose
boundary faces change) for remesh; the next gfx.vdraw does the work.

calls.name: gfx.vterrain
calls.prose:
Extrude a w*d byte
string of column heights (row-major) in ONE call. This is how a world gets
built: Lua does the noise, C does the filling.

calls.name: gfx.vworld
calls.prose:
Allocate the block grid. One per app
run; the world dies with the app. Cells are 1 byte, 0 = air, so 128x128x48
is 786KB of PSRAM where the same grid as a Lua table would blow the 2MB
heap. w and d must be multiples of chunk.

calls.name: gfx.zclear
calls.prose:
Reset the depth buffer to far (engine v16). For mesh scenes
with no ground pass (cards, mirrors) that still want z-tested models.

calls.name: vupp.ambience
calls.prose:
Loop assets/sfx/{name}.wav as a soft
background bed; vupp.ambience() (or nil) stops it. Engine v15. Idempotent:
calling every frame with the same bed is free, so apps can just assert the
ambience for their current scene in update(). Exempt from the politeness
limiter, the engine governs it instead: ONE bed at a time, volume hard-
capped soft (0.5), stopped by pause/suspend like every app voice (the
per-frame re-assert restarts it after resume).

params.name: name
params.constraint: sfx name only (no path, no extension)

calls.name: vupp.btn
calls.prose:
Is button `b` held right now? One of "up", "down",
"left", "right", "a", "b", "select"; an unknown name raises. "start" never
reaches an app, because the engine owns it for the pause menu (engine v7).
There
is no event queue: read the pad every frame.

calls.name: vupp.btnp
calls.prose:
Was `b` pressed on THIS frame? The edge, not the
level. Jumping, firing and moving a menu cursor want this one; walking
wants vupp.btn, and using btn where btnp belongs is why a menu selection
flies past six entries on one press.

calls.name: vupp.canvas.save
calls.prose:
Captures the CURRENT app canvas (or the `rect` region, canvas coords) ->
palette RGB565 -> 2x nearest-neighbor upscale (nicer viewing on phones) ->
JPEG beside the document as {doc_key}.jpg -> docstore document
{doc_type "drawing", payload, assets {"image":"{doc_key}.jpg"}, status
"queued", origin "device"} -> doc.put sync job (uploads the JPEG, upserts
the row). Re-saving the same key overwrites: the row id stays stable (like
the store doc), so newest wins locally and in the cloud (409->PATCH path).
Bad usage (oversized payload, bad key/rect) raises; I/O trouble returns
false (logged) so a full SD can't crash the app mid-masterpiece.

calls.name: vupp.date
calls.prose:
The real-world clock (engine v15): local date/time off the
battery-backed RTC through the policy tz table. Returns nil until the clock
has plausibly been set (epoch >= 2020), apps MUST handle nil (grow-style
per-visit fallbacks) since a fresh device may never have synced.

calls.name: vupp.docs.get
calls.prose:
One document from the
app's own namespace. nil when there is no such key, and also when the key
exists but holds a different doc_type.

calls.name: vupp.docs.list
calls.prose:
Every document of that
type in the app's own namespace, including the ones a parent pushed
(origin tells them apart). Each entry is {key, doc_type, status, origin,
payload}. Bounded to the newest 32, like the Messages screen.

calls.name: vupp.docs.of
calls.prose:
READ another app's documents (no isolation between
apps by design, docs/11; writes stay in the own namespace).

calls.name: vupp.docs.put
calls.prose:
Upsert into the
app's own namespace + queue the doc.put sync job.

calls.name: vupp.emit
calls.prose:
A note for the parent's activity feed, the thing
a parent actually opens the phone app to see. Emit at genuine milestones
such as "finished_level", "spelled_word" or "drawing.saved", never per frame.
payload is an optional small table; more than 512 bytes of JSON raises.

calls.name: vupp.import
calls.prose:
The only module
loader there is, since require/dofile/loadfile/load are removed from the
sandbox. Names are [a-z0-9_] with no path and no extension.

Results are cached for the life of the app, which is the point and also the
trap: whatever a module returns is pinned in the 2 MB Lua heap until the app
exits, so a lib file holding a big generated table costs that memory for the
whole run (see gfx.mload's .vmesh form for the way out). A module that
returns nothing caches as true, so it still only runs once.

calls.name: vupp.on_command
calls.prose:
Register fn(name, args) -> result table for the
commands the manifest declares (docs/11-app-contract.md). The runtime
handles acknowledgement and expiry; the app just answers.

calls.name: vupp.on_document
calls.prose:
Register fn(doc) for documents the PARENT pushes
while the app is running: a new colouring page, a word list, a photo. The
runtime calls it; the app never does. doc has the same shape vupp.docs.list
returns.

calls.name: vupp.quit
calls.prose:
Return to the launcher. Rarely the right call: since engine
v7 the START pause menu is how a child leaves an app, and an app that quits
itself takes that choice away mid-play.

calls.name: vupp.rand
calls.prose:
xorshift64* seeded once per run, which is the reason to prefer it over
math.random: a bug you hit reproduces on the next launch instead of
evaporating. math.random works and is not removed, but it does not have
that property.

calls.name: vupp.sfx
calls.prose:
Play assets/sfx/{name}.wav (16 kHz mono s16,
loudness-normalized at publish). Cached per app run.

params.name: name
params.constraint: sfx name only (no path, no extension)

calls.name: vupp.store.get

signatures.returns: the stored value, or `default` when the

calls.prose: Key was never written.

calls.name: vupp.store.set
calls.prose:
Value is nil | bool | number | string | small
table. Sugar over a single 'store' document underneath, so a high score is
parent-visible like everything else and survives both leaving the app and
reinstalling it. It also survives an edit, which is worth remembering while
testing a "best score".

The WHOLE store has to serialize into one document payload, so the size
check happens on the write rather than at flush time: an oversized value is
rolled back and raises, instead of quietly losing the save later. "store"
is a reserved document key. Keep it to a high score or the furthest level;
this is a save file, not a database.

calls.name: vupp.time
calls.prose:
Seconds of play since this app started, pauses
excluded. Not a wall clock and not comparable across runs: it is the clock
to drive animation and timers off. vupp.date() is the real-world one.

calls.name: vupp.tone
calls.prose:
A voice on the mixer. Waves:
"tri" (default, soft), "sine", "square" (chiptune), "saw", "noise".

calls.name: vupp.touch

signatures.returns: nil | {x, y, held} in canvas coordinates

calls.prose:
Held is true the
whole time a finger is down (apps do their own press-edge detection).
Only injected when the manifest declares the "touch" capability.

values.name: gfx.w
values.prose: Canvas width in pixels: 480 with "hires": true in app.json, 240 without. A plain number, not a call, so reading it is free.

values.name: gfx.h
values.prose: Canvas height in pixels: 320 hires, 160 legacy. A plain number, not a call.

globals.name: print
globals.prose: Goes to the device log tagged with the app slug. A child never sees it; the bench devconsole does.
